claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital for 12 weeks (within 12-week limit)
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex
expected_eligibility.reason: Claimant lives in the UK; Child is 8 (under 16); Child lives with claimant; Child is not in local authority care; Child in hospital for 12 weeks (within 12-week limit); Child is not fostered; Child does not work 24+ hours/week; Child has not started an apprenticeship in England; Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right
circumstances: Child is not in local authority care
Child in hospital for 12 weeks (within 12-week limit)
Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand the age of the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- Their age (or date of birth)
- If you have multiple children, please provide the age of each one

This will help me determine which path to follow in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old. I'm just wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Alex is 8 years old, so he falls into the under 16 category, which is great news - this means we can move forward with the assessment.

Let me continue through the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

This is checking whether he's involved in full-time work. Since Alex is 8 years old, he's likely not working, so this should be straightforward!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 8! He's in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I expected. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

Again, at 8 years old, he shouldn't be receiving these, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?**

Since he's only 8 years old and in primary school, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8 and in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is clearly not in any apprenticeship, so we can move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation, as this is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you normally live in the UK?** 

If you don't normally live in the UK, please let me know your immigration status or circumstances, as there are some special cases that may allow eligibility:
- Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- Do you have pre-settled status (and if so, are you working, studying, jobseeking, or have sufficient resources)?
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

Please describe your residency situation so I can determine if you meet the requirements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're based in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward - you normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirement. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check that you're responsible for Alex. This is important for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means either:
- You live with him, OR
- You contribute to his upkeep (e.g., pay for food, clothes, housing, pocket money), OR
- You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since Alex is your child and you're claiming for him, I assume you live with him and are responsible for his care. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You live with Alex, so you're clearly responsible for him. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim for him?**

For example:
- The other parent
- A grandparent
- Another relative or carer

If there is another claimant, have you agreed between yourselves who should be the main claimant?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him - it's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Where is Alex living?** Does any of the following apply:
- Is he currently in hospital?
- Is he in residential care?
- Is he being fostered?
- Or is he living at home normally?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for a few months now, actually. He's been quite poorly.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been unwell and is in hospital. Let me check the specific rules around hospital stays for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I need to understand the details of Alex's hospital stay to determine the rules that apply.

**Can you tell me:**
1. **How long has Alex been in hospital cumulatively?** (Please count all his hospital stays together. If he's been out for periods and then gone back in, I need to know if those gaps were less than 28 days - if so, those stays are added together)

2. **Has he had any previous hospital stays in the last few months?** If so, when did he come out, and when did he go back in (if applicable)?

The reason I'm asking is that Child Benefit has a special rule: you can receive it for up to 12 weeks while your child is in hospital. If the total time exceeds 12 weeks, different rules may apply.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in for about 3 months now - so that's around 12 weeks. It's been one continuous stay, he hasn't been home at all during this time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. So Alex has been in hospital for approximately 12 weeks continuously - that's right at the limit. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**While Alex is in hospital, are you regularly spending money on him?**

This could include things like:
- Visiting expenses (travel costs)
- Bringing him items (toys, books, comfort items, clothes)
- Paying for any personal items or services not covered by the hospital
- Any other regular contributions to his care or wellbeing while he's there

This is important because there's an exception to the 12-week rule if you're regularly spending money on the child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am - I still buy his clothes, magazines, and his favorite food to bring to him when I visit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's good - you're clearly supporting Alex while he's in hospital. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's hospital accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you responsible for paying for his care and accommodation, or is the council funding it?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - the NHS is covering his hospital care, but I'm still his parent and responsible for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's excellent news. Let me now provide you with the final outcome of your Child Benefit eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

Congratulations! You **are eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

---

### **Summary of Your Situation:**

✓ **Alex is 8 years old** - under the qualifying age of 16  
✓ **He's not working full-time** - he's in primary school  
✓ **He's not receiving disqualifying benefits** - no ESA or Universal Credit in his own name  
✓ **You live in the UK** - Manchester meets residency requirements  
✓ **You're responsible for him** - he lives with you  
✓ **No other claimant** - you're the sole person claiming for him  
✓ **Hospital stay exception applies** - Although Alex has been in hospital for approximately 12 weeks, because you're regularly spending money on his upkeep (clothes, magazines, food), the 12-week limit does not apply to you  
✓ **Local council not paying** - the NHS is covering his hospital care, which doesn't affect your Child Benefit entitlement

---

### **Next Steps:**

1. **Apply for Child Benefit** if you haven't already through:
   - **Online:** www.gov.uk/child-benefit-apply
   - **By phone:** 0808 100 2000
   - **By post:** Child Benefit Office, HM Revenue and Customs, Benton Park View, Newcastle upon Tyne, NE98 1ZZ

2. **You'll need:**
   - Your National Insurance number
   - Alex's date of birth and National Insurance number (if he has one)
   - Bank or building society details for payments

3. **Payments** are typically made weekly or every 4 weeks directly into your bank account

I hope Alex makes a full recovery soon. If you have any other questions about Child Benefit, feel free to ask!

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) He is under 16 years old (8 years old), which is a qualifying age; (2) He is not working full-time (he's in primary school); (3) He is not receiving benefits in his own right (ESA or Universal Credit); (4) He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) You normally live in the UK (Manchester) and meet residency requirements; (6) You live with Alex and are responsible for him; (7) No other person is claiming Child Benefit for him; (8) Although Alex has been in hospital for approximately 12 weeks (at the 12-week limit), you are regularly spending money on him while he's in hospital (clothes, magazines, food), which is an exception to the 12-week rule; (9) The local council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance - the NHS is covering his hospital care while you remain his parent and responsible for him. All eligibility criteria are satisfied.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. He meets all the qualifying criteria: he is under 16, not working full-time, not receiving disqualifying benefits, and you are responsible for him while normally residing in the UK. Although he has been in hospital for approximately 12 weeks, your regular spending on his upkeep (clothes, magazines, food) means the 12-week hospital limit does not apply. The NHS funding his hospital care does not affect your entitlement, as the local council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance. You should proceed with your Child Benefit claim."

response.question: Has the child's cumulative time in hospital or residential accommodation exceeded 12 weeks?
response.help_text: Child Benefit continues for up to 12 weeks in hospital/residential accommodation. CUMULATIVE RULE: If child returns within 28 days of leaving, time counts towards 12-week limit. Multiple stays within 28 days are added together.

criteria.calculation_method: Sum all hospital/residential stays. If gap between stays is less than 28 days, count both stays towards cumulative total. If gap is 28+ days, reset counter.
criteria.example: 10 weeks hospital + 15 day gap + 3 weeks hospital = 13 weeks cumulative (exceeds limit)

response.question: Are you regularly spending money on the child while they are in hospital/residential accommodation?
response.help_text: Exception to 12-week rule if you regularly spend money on child. For hospital abroad, only if they went abroad for treatment and you're back in UK. Partner's spending counts if married/civil partnered and living together.

response.help_text: You generally cannot get Child Benefit if the local council is paying for the child
